clue.text: See 11
See 11
Calling nurse, ankle finally bandaged up

indicators.note: something bandaged up is wrapped round, so the nurse word encloses the letter

parts.note: a carer is someone who nurses or looks after another

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word ankle

explanation.surface: A nurse is summoned to strap up an injured ankle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bandaged up' puts E, the last letter of 'ankle' (signalled by 'finally'), inside CARER.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a vocation or profession, which is what a career is.

clue.text: Paul's stout, kind of firm?

parts.note: Paul is the setter, so 'Paul's' is 'Paul is', from his own mouth I'M
porter is a dark beer, close kin to stout

explanation.surface: The setter describes himself as portly, or a business asks about its type.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often use their pseudonym for themselves: 'Paul's' becomes I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An importer is a type of company, one bringing goods in from abroad; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Supporter with popular, swell ideas

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
in means fashionable or popular
a swell at sea is made of waves

explanation.surface: A backer with a well-liked and excellent set of proposals.
explanation.definitionFit: Brainwaves are sudden clever thoughts, so they are inspired ideas.

clue.text: Young home help, OO I say?

indicators.note: I say means spoken out, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: two letter Os are 'O pair', a pair of Os

explanation.surface: An exclamation of mild surprise at a young domestic helper.
explanation.walkthrough: OO is a pair of Os, 'O pair', which spoken sounds like AU PAIR; 'I say' also doubles as a period exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young foreigner living with a family and helping with childcare and housework.

clue.text: Mushroom bake's filling consumed by Muslim

indicators.note: consumed by means eaten, so the filling goes inside the Muslim word

parts.note: a Shiite is a member of the Shia branch of Islam

indicators.note: the filling of a word is its inside, the letters between the ends

explanation.surface: A baked mushroom dish is eaten by a Muslim diner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling' signals the middle of the word, ignoring the possessive 's; 'consumed by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiitake is an edible fungus much used in East Asian cooking.

clue.text: Flight due, so desperately stealing kiss

indicators.note: stealing means taking in, so the shuffled letters hold the kiss
done desperately is done wildly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: X is the kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A flight is due, so someone is frantically grabbing a farewell kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desperately' scrambles the two words to EODUS, and 'stealing' takes the kiss inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An exodus is a mass departure, a flight of people from somewhere.

clue.text: Quiet sound as a double knocked back?

indicators.note: knocked back reads as turned back, so the letters run in reverse

parts.note: the spirit is unnamed: the question mark lets the drink be taken as rum, the classic sailor's tot
a double is a second measure of the same spirit poured in, so rum once more

explanation.surface: A soft noise comes from someone downing a double measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' looks like drinking but reverses the letters; the question mark admits that the spirit, rum, is only implied by the double.
explanation.definitionFit: A murmur is a low, soft, indistinct noise, such as hushed speech.

clue.text: State of Connecticut a horror

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the answer sits inside the following words

explanation.surface: One American state seems a nightmare to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' signals letters taken from inside: connectiCUT A Horror holds UTAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is one of the fifty United States, west of Colorado.

clue.text: Lying on cloth, white meat I cut, odd bits of herb scattered about

indicators.note: scattered about means strewn around, so all these letters are rearranged
the odd bits of a word are its first, third and so on letters

explanation.surface: A cooking scene: white meat sliced on a cloth with herbs strewn around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' herb gives HR; 'scattered about' rearranges ONCLOTHWHITEMEATICUT plus HR into ECONOMICAL WITH THE TRUTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Being economical with the truth is a polite idiom for being deceptive, telling less than the full facts.

clue.text: Reportedly plod back

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to lumber is to move heavily and clumsily, to plod

explanation.surface: Word has it that someone trudged home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' gives LUMBER said aloud; 'back' looks like a direction but is an adjective here, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumbar describes the lower part of the spine, so it means relating to the back.

clue.text: Stick turned wheels secured by nuts

indicators.note: secured by means held in, so the reversed word sits inside

parts.note: barking, as in barking mad, means crazy, nuts

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: A rod, rotated, has wheels fastened with nuts, like an axle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' is criticism, as in British 'giving someone stick'; 'turned' is the reversal and 'secured by' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracking is noisy jeering and heckling, the abuse also called stick in British slang.

clue.text: Tug circled by cruisers getting bow clipped — that's inauspicious

indicators.note: circled by means surrounded, so the tug word goes inside
the bow is a ship's front, so the first letter of the line's name is cut off

parts.note: Cunard is the shipping line whose liners make cruises
to tug is to pull, or tow

explanation.surface: A tugboat surrounded by cruise liners loses its prow, an unlucky outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Cunard is the British line famous for ocean liners; 'getting bow clipped' leaves UNARD, and 'circled by' wraps it round the tug word.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unfavourable or unfortunate, so it can describe an unpromising, ill-omened event.

clue.text: Exhausting at university struggling to make ends meet

parts.note: hard work is exhausting
up means at university, as in being up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A tiring student life spent short of cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard up is an idiom for short of money, struggling to cover living costs.

clue.text: See 24 across
See 22 down
Saw is, after all, not quite cutting grass

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so these letters go inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

indicators.note: after puts the word is behind the shortened word
not quite means falling short, so the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A saw, after all, is not really for cutting grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' shortens 'all', 'after' places 'is' behind it, and 'cutting' puts the resulting ALIS inside the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: To realise something is to understand it, as in 'I saw what you meant'.

clue.text: Garment is resurrected?

definitions.meaning: underwear, a garment worn beneath clothes
read as ..., one who ... comes back to life

explanation.surface: A piece of clothing makes an unlikely comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is whimsical: split as UN-DIES, the reverse of dying, which is being resurrected; the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Undies is a casual word for underwear, the clothes worn next to the skin.

clue.text: Ninja elected by Charlie and Wally

parts.note: a charlie is a fool, an ass
a wally is a fool, an ass
a winning candidate is in

explanation.surface: A martial-arts fighter is voted in by two men named Charlie and Wally.
explanation.walkthrough: Charlie and Wally are British slang for a fool, both ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese warrior trained in espionage and covert killing.

clue.text: Setter imbibing drink way down in Austria?

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so the setter word takes the drink inside

parts.note: the sun is something that sets each evening
kir is white wine with blackcurrant liqueur

explanation.surface: The crossword setter enjoys a drink on holiday in the Alps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' looks like the puzzle's compiler but is the sun, which sets; 'imbibing' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski run is a slope or track skiers descend, the sort found in Austrian resorts.

clue.text: Get lost following European character in Asian capital

indicators.note: following puts the get-lost word after the Greek letter

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a European character
scat is an order to go away

explanation.surface: Someone from Europe is told to leave an Asian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital city of Oman, on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Player, owner of small vehicle, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means spoken out loud, so the words are taken by sound

parts.note: one who drives a Mini, the small British car

explanation.surface: A game player turns out to have a tiny car.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a small classic British car.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnie Driver is an English actress, and a player is an actor on stage or screen.

clue.text: Nine kids author Charles initially mistreated — shabby of him?

indicators.note: mistreated means badly handled, so these letters are knocked into a new order
initially points to the first letters of author and Charles

explanation.surface: Accusing the author Charles of neglecting his many children, a shabby act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives A and C; 'mistreated' rearranges NINEKIDS plus AC. 'him' points to Dickens, the author in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickensian describes squalid, poverty-stricken conditions like those in Charles Dickens's novels, hence shabby in his manner.

clue.text: 21 November this year says: 'I turn pud when mixing'

indicators.note: mixing means stirring together, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A date speaks, claiming it is when puddings get stirred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when mixing' rearranges SAYSITURNPUD. Stir-up Sunday, the last before Advent, is when British families traditionally make the Christmas pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir-up Sunday is the Sunday before Advent, which fell on 21 November that year.

clue.text: Team's wing

definitions.meaning: a wing or flank, as of a building or army

explanation.definitionFit: A football side is a team, and a wing is one side of a building or army.

clue.text: African country spent money?

definitions.meaning: A nation on Africa's west coast
an old British coin, money now out of use

explanation.definitionFit: Guinea is a West African state, and the guinea was a former British coin worth 21 shillings.

clue.text: Mould blocking drain on the surface

indicators.note: blocking means stuck in the middle, so the mould word goes inside

parts.note: to seep is to drain away slowly
a mould is a type or kind, as in 'cast in the same mould'

explanation.surface: Fungus clogging a drain only on its surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mould' looks like fungus but means type, as in 'cast in the same mould'; 'blocking' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin-deep means superficial, going no further than the outward appearance.
